ES6.0	PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY ~
Safety is integral to the operations at the Woodland Facility. Implementing safety improvements is an on-going process at the Facility. Grow West conducts periodic evaluations to assess the effectiveness of the maintenance and safety programs. Specific changes to the anhydrous ammonia and aqua ammonia processes at the Facility will be implemented as needed.
~~~~~

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
||
ES1.0	FACILITY ACCIDENTAL RELEASE POLICY ~
The owners, management, and employees of Grow West | Woodland Wholesale (herein referred to as Woodland Facility or Facility) are committed to the prevention of accidental releases of anhydrous ammonia or aqua ammonia. Grow West has prepared this Risk Management Plan (RMP) in accordance with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA) Program regulations to address process and operational safety. 
||
If an accidental release were to occur, the Facility is prepared to work with the local fire department, or other authorities, to mitigate the release and to minimize the impact of the release on people and the environment. A detailed Emergency Response Program (ERP) has been developed and will be implemented in the event of an accidental release. 
||
ES2.0	FACILITY INFORMATION ~
The Woodland Facility provides fertilizers and related products to farmers and other agricultural supply operations. The Facilitys primary activity is the sale of liquid fertilizers, including anhydrous ammonia and aqua ammonia; granular fertilizers (prill); and a variety of non bulk, pre packaged chemicals (e.g., herbicides and pesticides) to farmers in the Sacramento Valley of Northern California. The applicable NAICS code for this facility is 42491 (Farm Supplies Merchant Wholesalers). The Woodland Facility is not co-located within one mile from another regulated facility and has not had a reportable accident within the last five years. No practicability assessment for inherently safer technology or design (IST/ISD) is required.
||
The Woodland Facility has been assigned the U.S. EPA Facility Identifier number 1000-0002-8846 and has a physical address of 40189 County Road 18C, Woodland, California 95776.
||
Anhydrous Ammonia
||
- The maximum amount of anhydrous ammonia in inventory exceeds the U.S. EPA regulatory threshold of 10,000 lbs. 
||
- Anhydrous ammonia, as a liquefied compressed gas, will boil under ambient

atmospheric conditions. Liquid ammonia will expand by 850 times when it evaporates. 
||
- The Woodland Facility sells anhydrous ammonia for direct application, via U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) nurse tanks, as a crop nutrient. The Woodland Facility does not fill nurse tanks; the nurse tanks are filled at other Grow West properties. 
||
- Anhydrous ammonia may be present at the Woodland Facility in DOT approved nurse tanks. The nurse tanks have a water capacity of 1,000 gallons but are filled with no more than 850 gallons of anhydrous ammonia. The Woodland Facility will have no more than three loaded nurse tanks at the property at one time. 
||
- The DOT nurse tanks are returned empty from client sites. The empty nurse tanks may contain a de minimis amount of ammonia present (effectively empty) and are not considered part of the inventory. 
||
- The maximum quantity of anhydrous ammonia handled is 13,107 pounds.

Aqua Ammonia 
||

||

||

ES3.0	ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM ~
The Facility has implemented the following prevention program elements. 
||
Process Safety Information (PL3) | Safety Information (PL2). ~
The Facility ensures that information concerning covered processes and regulated substances are up-to-date and available for review by employees. Safety Information includes Safety Data Sheets (SDSs), chemical inventories, operating limits (temperatures, pressures, flows, compositions), equipment specifications, and Codes and Standards used to design, build, and operate the process. For PL3, the information includes block flow and piping and instrument diagrams (P&IDs) (where applicable), descriptions of safety systems, and materials of construction information for the installed systems. 
||
Process Hazards Analysis (PL3) | Hazard Review (PL2). ~
A review of the ammonia processes is conducted every five years or as needed following a process change. A review of the results from the most recent hazard review for the anhydrous ammonia process and aqua ammonia process indicated that no high-risk hazards were identified by the review team.
||
Operating Procedures ~
Written operating procedures have been developed for the covered processes. The operating procedures for the anhydrous ammonia are reviewed and recertified on an annual basis. The operating procedures for aqua ammonia are reviewed, updated, as necessary to reflect current practice, or whenever the tasks or steps to perform on the covered process are found to be inadequate or inaccurate.
|| 
Training ~
Facility personnel and Grow West corporate management understand that incidents involving the accidental release of regulated substances can be reduced by having adequately trained operations and maintenance (O&M) personnel. A training program, which incorporates operating procedures and safe work practices, is an essential element of an effective prevention pr

ogram. The current training program is comprised of the following:
- Initial employee training.
- Periodic refresher training.
- Training provided for new equipment additions or modifications.
- Competency testing involving written tests and observation following training; and
- Training records for each employee.
||
Mechanical Integrity (PL3) And Maintenance (PL2). ~
The Woodland Facility has implemented a Mechanical Integrity / Maintenance program for its regulated substances. The program at the Facility is intended to preserve the mechanical integrity of the process equipment to minimize the potential for an accidental release. The program includes equipment inspection, preventive maintenance, recordkeeping, and training and is conducted in accordance with manufacturers requirements and industry practices (e.g., Recognized and Generally Accepted Good Engineering Practices, RAGAGEP). 
||
Management Of Change (PL3) ~
Operational, safety, and environmental issues must be reviewed prior to the initiation of a process change to ensure that they do not compromise the safety and integrity of the Anhydrous Ammonia Process, and to minimize adverse effects to worker safety and public health. The Management of Change (MOC) procedures are used to evaluate changes to process materials, controls, equipment, and procedures.
||
Pre-Startup Safety Review (PL3) ~
The pre-startup safety review (PSSR) applies to additions or modifications to the Anhydrous Ammonia Process that require the safety information to be revised or updated. As changes in affected processes are identified or planned, they must be evaluated and a PSSR completed if deemed necessary in accordance with operating procedures. The assessment is undertaken in conjunction with the MOC review. A PSSR is performed in conjunction with the MOC review process when the proposed change requires modifications to the safety or operational procedures.
||
Compliance Audits. ~
Grow West conducts triennial compliance audits of th

e RMP program to assess the effectiveness of the written plan and to identify gaps in the program. Records of the audits and follow-up documentation are maintained to indicate findings and resolution of findings. 
||
Incident Investigation. ~
Although no incidents involving regulated substances have occurred at the Facility in the last five years, Grow West has an incident investigation program and documentation in place. The program includes investigation requirements and reporting and would be implemented in the event of an incident.
||
Employee Participation (PL3) ~
The Facility must rely upon the operational expertise and training of its employees at all levels and disciplines to ensure safe operations. The Facility has an Employee Participation Program in place and has implemented procedures regarding engaging employees for their input, providing access to safety documentation, and seeking employee knowledge and experience in applicable areas of the program.
||
Hot Work Permit (PL3). ~
For hot work that may occur on or near the Anhydrous Ammonia Process, Grow West has developed a written Hot Work Permit program and procedure to document the requirements to complete the work and provide adequate fire prevention and process protection. 
||
Contractor Safety (PL3).
The contractors used by the Facility for anhydrous ammonia services have been informed regarding the known potential fire, explosion, or toxic release hazards related to anhydrous ammonia at the Facility. The Facility qualifies contractors who are engaged in maintaining the RS systems to ensure that equipment is properly repaired and returned to service safely.
||

ES4.0	FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY ~
There have been no accidental releases of anhydrous ammonia, aqua ammonia, or regulated pesticides during the last five years resulting in death, injuries, evacuations, shelter in-place orders, or property or environmental damage.
||
